heroHeadline: Scottish Parliament Passes Section 30 Demand 72-55; BoE Bailey Signals Inflation Tolerance as Parliament Returns
heroSubtitle: The Scottish Parliament voted 72 to 55 on 26 May to demand the UK Government grant a Section 30 order for an independence referendum — the largest pro-independence parliamentary majority in Holyrood's history — but Westminster under Starmer rejected the request immediately. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey, speaking at the Reykjavik 2026 economic conference on 29 May, signalled the BoE could tolerate above-target inflation temporarily to support the UK's weak economy, raising expectations of a June rate cut ahead of the next MPC meeting on 18 June. Parliament returns from Whitsun Recess on 1 June with the NHS Modernisation Bill — which proposes abolishing NHS England and integrating its functions into the DHSC — set for its second reading as first major business. Labour's leadership crisis continues to simmer with LabourList tracking showing 98 MPs demanding Starmer's resignation against 159 backing him, as the Prime Minister prepares to face Parliament again.
footerNote: Data sourced from UK Parliament Hansard, The National Archives, ONS, Bank of England, Electoral Commission, NHS England, BBC, Reuters, FT, The Guardian, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, CNN, CNBC, ITV News, SPICe, and major academic institutions including LSE, Chatham House, and the Resolution Foundation.
